rv.q: Unfortunately, though, the additions don't deepen Odets's play as much as bloat it in an attempt to hammer home the drivers' struggle as representative of all workers', then and now.
The abstraction clashes with Odets’ literal depictions of the working poor.

cn.t: Steven Pasquale's musical take on Odets' 1935 labor drama delivers a rousing rallying cry for workers' rights, though critics find the agitprop style shows its age despite the timeless relevance of economic injustice.

vr.q: This is a pretty successful exercise in elevating an otherwise cold and distant piece.
